where: the hint under 'Approve this kiosk' (y=352-391) and the first item of 'If the kiosk still waits' (y=536-575) — both above the fold, 145px apart, on a page that only has four things on it
finding: The section arrived on the counselor's page this round and kept the rank it had when it was tertiary reference in an admin's right-hand column. Two costs for the person the journey says is actually standing there at 6:40pm. First, its opening item repeats, in different words, the sentence she read twenty seconds earlier under the button: 'Codes last ten minutes. If this one is refused, read the code the kiosk is showing now and try again.' then 'A code expires ten minutes after the kiosk shows it. Read the one on screen now.' On a page this short both are in the same glance, and a list whose first entry is something the reader has already been told is a list she stops reading — which costs her items two and three, the home-screen-install second pairing and the deactivated approver, the two causes she has no other way of learning and the whole reason the section was ungated. Second, those three items are set at 12px ink-400, one step below the 14px hint above them, making the only troubleshooting content she will ever get the smallest informational type on her screen, read in a dim hallway while she looks back and forth at an iPad across the room. On the admin build the same 12px is right, because it sits under three louder registers and the same duplicate pair is 590px apart; on hers the section is half the page.

direction: Two separate edits, neither structural. Cut the redundancy at whichever end is cheaper — the under-button hint can lose its second sentence, since the list now carries the stale-code case for both roles, or the list's first item can go. And on the build with no core section, let the list sit at the page's body register (14px, ink-300/ink-400) rather than the reference register it inherited; the shared-component rule is satisfied by a role difference, not a global size change, so the admin's dense column is untouched.

where: the last footnote paragraph, y=797-856, 12px ink-500, the bottom of the counselor's page
finding: The retirement footnote was made identical to the admin's this round, and its second half names a control a counselor does not have: 'or deactivate and reactivate your account to cut every session loose.' Deactivation lives on the Team screen, which is core-gated and which she cannot open, and it is not something she can do to herself from anywhere in the app. The cost is small because the first clause — clear the browser's site data on the device — is a thing she can do, and because retiring a kiosk is not the 6:40pm job at all. But it is the second instruction on this page that points a counselor at something she cannot reach, and the whole point of the scene was to stop doing that.
evidence: kiosk-setup-counselor--phone.html and kiosk-menu-counselor--phone.html carry the admin string verbatim: 'To retire a kiosk, clear the browser's site data on the device — or deactivate and reactivate your account to cut every session loose.' Rendered at 12px rgb(100,116,139), y=797-856 on a 903px page, so it is the last thing before the fold and the only thing that scrolls. Grep confirms all five phone scenes now share one sentence.
direction: Let the clause be role-conditional, the way the section gating already is: the counselor keeps the site-data half, which is the half she can act on. The constraint that diagnostics stay core-team does not touch this — it is prose, not a call — so this is only a matter of not shipping one role's capability as another role's instruction.
